dataVersion.description: Monotonic schema version for extension-owned settings/KV/cache interpretation. The host commits it only after successful registration.

runtime.description: Required execution boundary. New distributable Swift extensions should use webAssembly; native must be selected explicitly and is retained only for deprecated compatibility.

executable.description: Manifest-relative path. Absolute paths and '.' or '..' components are invalid.

capabilities.description: Safe WebAssembly v1 values include commands, panels, mcp.tools, settings, services.provide, services.consume, facts.provide, source-control.read, companions.invoke, ui.components, ui.workspace-navigation, ui.rendering.metal, ui.media-documents, attachments.preview, attachments.file-types, appearance.provider-icons, appearance.account-icons, appearance.session-identity, appearance.themes, appearance.fonts, host.projects.read, host.project.files.read, host.sessions.read, host.sessions.runtime.read, host.repositories.read, host.providers.read, host.accounts.presentation.read, host.events, storage.kv, storage.cache, storage.secrets, and network.brokered (paired with explicit networkGrants). source-control.read is paired with sourceControlProviders and permits only connection-scoped GET/HEAD requests beneath a declared API prefix; Threading selects the exact HTTPS origin and attaches its Keychain credential. facts.provide publishes bounded scalar facts only against boundary-safe repository domain keys; it grants no project or session read authority. appearance.themes and appearance.fonts are data-plane: the host reads the declared documents and font files itself, and the running extension gains no new broker operation from either. companions.invoke addresses only operations declared by the same extension's companion. ui.workspace-navigation registers semantic navigator documents but grants no additional host-data authority. ui.rendering.metal permits constrained host-owned custom surfaces only; it does not grant Metal objects to the extension process. ui.media-documents permits a `media` node — a document handle plus a playback intent, drawn by a host-owned player; no decoder, surface or pixel reaches the extension. attachments.preview permits offering a preview body for one attachment and grants no attachment read authority: a candidate learns an attachment's name, kind, size, origin and the host's content hint and nothing more. attachments.file-types adds file extensions to the attachments scanner's allow-list and may not claim an extension Threading already classifies. host.project.files.read returns opaque, generation-bound content handles plus bounded filesystem metadata — name, project-relative path, byte size, modification date, content hint — and never bytes or an absolute path; it is not implied by host.projects.read. host.sessions.runtime.read returns only host-attributed process and listening-port rows for an exact session ID; it does not grant process-table access. network.client is reserved for deprecated native compatibility and is rejected for WebAssembly; brokered fetches through networkGrants replace it. Unknown values remain inspectable but are rejected by hosts that do not support them.

workspaceNavigators.description: Static host-evaluated navigator declarations. Every value must contain a pipeline and the running generation must register the exact same declaration. Materialized v1 navigators remain runtime-only for compatibility. Requires ui.workspace-navigation.

factDefinitions.description: Domain-keyed scalar facts this process generation may publish. Requires facts.provide.

sourceControlProviders.description: Read-only hosted-Git adapters. Requires source-control.read and exact manifest/registration parity. Origins and credentials are host-configured, never declared here.

companions.description: Optional separately signed macOS worker apps. Companions extend a WebAssembly core; they do not replace its settings, commands, panels, hooks, tools, storage, or host-data capability boundary.

networkGrants.description: Origins the network.brokered capability may fetch from, shown verbatim in the install dialog. Every fetch runs host-side; the guest gains no socket. v1 grants are https-only exact DNS hosts with GET/HEAD. Redirects are followed only when HTTPS, host, method, absent port, and absent user info remain inside that same grant; any other redirect returns its original 3xx for a new independently checked request. A grant naming a credential provider (v1: github) is served with the user's best connected credential — app connection, gh CLI, git credential helper, anonymous — and the response reports which tier answered; tokens never reach the extension. A credentialed grant is refused when the manifest also declares a companion holding network.client.

host.description: Exact lowercase DNS name — no scheme, wildcard, port, or path.

credential.description: A host-known credential provider whose connected credential the broker attaches.

themes.description: App-theme documents offered to the host's theme library while the extension is enabled. Requires the appearance.themes capability. Each resource is a package-relative JSON file in the host's app-theme vocabulary (the document Threading stores for a custom theme); the host reads, validates, and namespaces it (ext.<extension>.<id>) at inspection time, before any extension code runs.

fonts.description: Font files (.otf, .ttf, .ttc) registered process-scoped for Threading's own chrome while the extension is enabled. Requires the appearance.fonts capability. Family names come from the files themselves; the host parses each file at inspection time and names every family in the install disclosure. Licensing of a bundled font is the package author's responsibility.

localizations.description: Optional package-owned translation tables. Each resource is a flat JSON object mapping base-language presentation strings to translations. The host negotiates against the user's preferred languages, localizes host-rendered contributions, and supplies the same selected table to the extension process.

bundlePath.description: Package-relative path to a nested app. The host rejects absolute paths, '.', '..', symlink escapes, malformed bundles, and mismatched derived bundle identifiers.

capabilities.description: OS-facing companion authority, independently approved from the WebAssembly core's Threading host capabilities. SDK v1 values are background.service, process.spawn, network.client, network.listen, filesystem.user-selected.read, filesystem.user-selected.write, screen.capture, input.control, automation.apple-events, notifications.post, clipboard.read, clipboard.write, and ui.remote-surfaces.

operations.description: Named, schema-described operations the WebAssembly core may invoke through Threading's host broker. Declaring any operation requires the core capability companions.invoke.

surfaces.description: Bounded pixel surfaces rendered by this companion into host-owned views. Declaring any surface requires the companion capability ui.remote-surfaces.

accessibilityLabel.description: Host-owned accessibility fallback for the pixel surface.
